item.title: Rahm backs player freedom after LIV defections
item.description: Jon Rahm says golfers should be free to choose to play "where they want", following the latest defection from LIV Golf ahead of the season opener in Riyadh this week.

item.title: Westwood to miss opening LIV Golf events
item.description: Lee Westwood will miss the opening two events of the 2026 LIV Golf season after withdrawing due to a wrist injury.

item.title: LIV Golf unhappy with ranking points ‘restriction’
item.description: LIV Golf has welcomed the Official World Golf Ranking’s decision to award points to its events from 2026, but says the move does not go far enough.

item.title: Sattelkau sets early pace at Humewood
item.description: Germany’s Celina Sattelkau carded a three-under 69 to lead the SuperSport Ladies Challenge after a delayed opening round at Humewood Golf Club.

item.title: Detry, Uihlein lead as Oosthuizen lurks in Riyadh
item.description: Thomas Detry shrugged off debut nerves to share the first-round lead at LIV Golf Riyadh, with South Africa’s Louis Oosthuizen two shots behind.

item.title: Scheffler happy to have Koepka back
item.description: Top-ranked Scottie Scheffler sees the return of LIV Golf players to the PGA Tour as a start to having the world's best talent competing beyond Major events.

item.title: Reed, Hillier continue fine form to share Qatar lead
item.description: Patrick Reed continued his stunning start to the season to share the first-round lead with Daniel Hillier at the Qatar Masters.

item.title: Pace on McClymont’s heels at Humewood
item.description: Scotland’s Lorna McClymont will take a two-stroke lead into Friday’s final round of the SuperSport Ladies Challenge.

item.title: Magnificent seven share Cape Town Open lead
item.description: The first-round leaderboard of the CIRCA Cape Town Open resembled the peak holiday queue for the cable car up Table Mountain. MICHAEL VLISMAS reports. Seven players finished tied for the lead on seven under par at Royal Cape Golf Club on Thursday. item.title: Gotterup leads Phoenix Open, Scheffler struggles
item.description: Chris Gotterup is off to another hot start in his bid to claim a second PGA Tour title of 2026 at the Phoenix Open.
